claims.text: The FeNiCrMn alloy is equiatomic, Co-free, single-phase, and in a solidified solid-solution state.
Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi enhances local short-range atomic ordering.
Short-range atomic ordering affects the local stacking-fault energy.
Co removal alters the temperature dependence of stacking-fault energy in FeNiCrMn.
Changes in local stacking-fault energy modulate dislocation mobility.
Enhanced short-range order modifies the local energy landscape experienced by dislocations.
The stacking-fault-energy adjustment changes the balance between dislocation nucleation and dislocation motion.
The proposed changes in ordering, stacking-fault energy, and dislocation behavior produce dynamic strain-aging effects.
These dynamic strain-aging effects sustain increased strength without compromising ductility under specific temperature and strain-rate conditions.
Under identical conditions, Co-free FeNiCrMn will have a more robust strength–ductility balance than equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, particularly at intermediate temperatures and strain rates.
The Co-free alloy will exhibit more short-range ordering than the Co-containing baseline, and the increased ordering will correlate with improved mechanical performance.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has standard short-range order and corresponding stacking-fault energies that produce conventional dislocation dynamics.
Cryogenic temperatures limit diffusion, whereas moderately elevated temperatures provide atomic mobility that can facilitate short-range ordering.
The proposed mechanism applies only when temperature permits diffusion and ordering without activating competing high-temperature deformation mechanisms.
The proposed mechanism applies over strain rates that can capture dynamic strain aging but excludes extreme rates dominated by inertial effects.
